items.title: Hackers publish thousands of drivers’ data after breaching Florida motor vehicle database
items.summary: The ShinyHunters gang leaked the files online after saying the Florida state agency did not pay their ransom demand.

items.title: Your AI agents can now control your Google Home devices
items.summary: Google is launching early access to a new MCP server for Google Home, allowing AI agents like Claude, ChatGPT, and others to control connected devices, review camera summaries, and access smart home activity using natural language.

items.title: Anthropic merges Claude chat and Cowork in one interface
items.summary: Anthropic is initially releasing these features to Pro and Max plan subscribers.

items.title: Hear why Neuralink co-founder Max Hodak says the screen era is ending at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
items.summary: At this year's Disrupt, Neuralink's co-founder Max Hodak will present a vision for screen-free interfaces that can even offer medical help. Register before September 25 to save up to $200 on your pass.

items.title: How Fortell is using AI (and $163M) to crack a hearing aid monopoly
items.summary: “Why do I have to beg my grandparents to put on their hearing aids, but no one has ever needed to ask me to put on my glasses?” That’s the question that drove Matthew de Jonge to spend six years building Fortell, an AI hearing aid startup that recently raised $163 million from the likes of Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, and Valor Equity […]

items.title: May Mobility is going public in a $1.4B SPAC deal
items.summary: The deal could net the asset-light robotaxi company more than $300 million in funding.

items.title: Robots are waiting for a ChatGPT moment: Nvidia’s Les Karpas explains why at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
items.summary: The robotics industry is still waiting for their breakthrough into day-to-day life. Nvidia's Les Karpas has an answer as to why at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Register before September 25 to save up to $200 on your pass.

items.title: Google says some Pixel phone owners were hacked in zero-day attacks
items.summary: The Pixel phone maker said there are indications that a bug in the phone's modem "may be under limited, targeted exploitation."

items.title: Amazon gives its workers a raise of $1 per hour
items.summary: Amazon's investment in these raises comes out to over $1.5 billion, or about 0.06% of its $2.68 trillion market cap.

items.title: Threads’ new features let podcasters promote shows and reach listeners
items.summary: Threads is rolling out new tools for podcasters, including profile cards, episode links, transcripts, guest tags, posting reminders, and audience insights, as Meta looks to make the X rival a bigger hub for podcast promotion and discussion.

items.title: Next wave of VCs judging Startup Battlefield 200 contenders at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 revealed
items.summary: Meet the next five top-tier investors judging the Startup Battlefield 200 contenders live at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026. Register before September 25 to save up to $200 and don't miss a moment of the ultimate startup pitch competition.

items.title: 3 days left to exhibit: Get your brand in front of VCs and high-value leads at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
items.summary: Last day to book your exhibit table at Disrupt is September 18. Three days left. Get your startup in front of 10,000+ founders, investors, operators, and tech leaders on October 13–15.

items.title: SK Hynix reportedly in talks with Intel to build memory chips in US
items.summary: SK Hynix told TechCrunch the company hasn't finalized any plans or arrangements yet.

items.title: Former Infosys chief’s AI startup nabs another $53M
items.summary: The Palo Alto startup says it has landed multiple seven-figure enterprise contracts within months of launch.

items.title: Clean tech startup Fluxnium found a way to tap 50,000 years’ worth of nuclear fuel
items.summary: Fluxnium's fibers can extract uranium directly from seawater, which has enough of the nuclear fuel to power thousands of generations.

items.title: Amazon launches Alexa+ in India with Hindi support
items.summary: Amazon is letting all customers use Alexa+ assistant in early access period.

items.title: We don’t need AI regulation — leave safety to us, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says
items.summary: AI isn't some new form of "alien mind," according to Jensen Huang. It's just hardware and software, so safety can be engineered by each AI product maker.

items.title: The AI data center boom is colliding with cities scarred by big industry
items.summary: National outcry against data center construction has spread to Philadelphia, where officials suggested possible construction in a neighborhood already impacted by a now-defunct oil refinery.

items.title: Meta now lets AI agents handle the boring parts of WhatsApp Business setup
items.summary: A new WhatsApp Business MCP server lets developers use AI coding agents like Claude, Cursor, Codex, and ChatGPT to handle setup, messaging templates, testing, and troubleshooting.

items.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
items.summary: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
